summary: The article surveys local efforts on substance abuse prevention and recovery, rooted in the view that socioeconomic factors such as unemployment, housing instability and lack of education drive addiction. It covers youth prevention programs, low-cost recovery services, business-led job support, diverse support groups, holistic rehabilitation and a community training program. Local experts stress accessibility, collaboration and addressing the whole person.
one_line: Local programs tackle substance abuse through socioeconomic-aware prevention, accessible recovery, support groups, holistic care and community training in 2023.
key_facts: Dr. Karen Thomas, an epidemiologist, said at a September panel at the Wilson Community Center that people in lower socioeconomic brackets often experience higher rates of substance abuse due to environmental stressors, limited resources and systemic barriers.
Social worker John Bentley said exposure to high-crime neighborhoods and drugs in the community is "like a trap that's set and waiting."
Local prevention programs began implementation following a grant awarded on September 15, 2023.
Susan Alvarez, director of the Eastside Prevention Initiative, leads a campaign educating youths about substance use risks through schools, workshops and community outreach.
The Youth Mentorship Program, started by former teacher James Peterson, pairs at-risk youths with mentors from various professional backgrounds.
The New Beginnings Recovery Center opened on October 10, 2023, under director Dr. Lisa Rodriguez; its services are low-cost and in some cases free.
New Beginnings offers medical detoxification, counseling, group therapy and help with socioeconomic issues, with partnerships with local job centers and housing agencies.
Entrepreneur Michael Chapman led local businesses in launching the Community Care Coalition in late September 2023 to provide jobs and training for people in recovery.
A Thursday support group at the Serenity Wellness Clinic, facilitated by clinical psychologist Maria Gomez, brings together members from various socioeconomic backgrounds.
Dr. Henry Clark's holistic program at the Evergreen Rehabilitation Facility launched on November 1, 2023, and includes nutritional guidance, physical therapy and mental health services.
A training program coordinated by Dr. Elaine Sanders rolled out at the end of 2023 for health professionals, community leaders and residents to identify early signs of substance abuse.
Training sessions cover navigating insurance and healthcare for treatment and understanding the psychological underpinnings of addiction.
